planting_details.assumptions_or_notes: Assumes rainfed smallholder system in Kitale with main long-rains season planting (late March–early April); H614 is a late-maturing hybrid suited to high rainfall/high altitude. Population derived from 0.75 m row spacing and ~0.30 m within-row spacing (1 plant/hill after thinning). Planting depth set for medium-sized seed in moist soils. Row orientation unknown; 0° used as a standard default. Local practice and recommendations from Kenyan highland maize agronomy inform values.

events.Assumptions_or_Notes: Diammonium phosphate (DAP, 18-46-0) band-placed near seed at planting, ~5 cm depth. Representative local practice in Kitale uses DAP as basal P with some starter N. Product rate assumed 125 kg/ha → N = 125×0.18 = 22.5 kg/ha; P2O5 = 125×0.46 = 57.5 kg/ha; elemental P = 57.5×0.4364 ≈ 25.1 kg/ha. No K added. Placement approximates band/spot in furrow common for smallholder/medium farms.

Calcium ammonium nitrate (CAN, ~26% N) topdressed by hand broadcast at ~V6 (first weeding), a common practice in Trans-Nzoia. N set to 67.5 kg/ha so that seasonal N totals exactly 90 kg/ha. Implied product ≈ 67.5/0.26 ≈ 260 kg/ha. Often broadcast between rows; sometimes lightly incorporated by weeding. No P or K applied in this topdress.
